newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, Ssangyong trouble affects.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, Ssangyong trouble affects.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed marginally higher on Wednesday, but sentiment turned bearish due to financial difficulties with Ssangyong Motor and the Jinro Group, brokers said.
Profit-taking emerged on blue chips, including petrochimicals, which rose recently on falling international naphtha prices, while theme-backed small shares picked up.
"The 700 level is quite sticky. Investors became defensive as the index failed to take off from the floor," said Lim Sung-woon, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
The composite index ended 1.03 points higher at 702.42.
Ssangyong Motor said it was considering selling its headquarter building and other assets to pay off heavy debts.
Ssangyong's surprise announcement follows a similar asset sale plan unveiled on Tuesday by the Jinro Group.
Analysts said Ssangyong accumulated 3.7 trillion won of debts after investing heavily to develop new vehicles, paying more than 300 billion won annually in interest.
The company put its debts at 3.2 trillion won.
Trading volume totalled 39.05 million shares, compared with 46.72 million on Tuesday. Advanders outpaced losers 452 to 346, with 111 unchanged.
Brokers said theme-backed small shares were demanded despite an overall bearish tone. Tae Heung Leather rose 1,300 won to its limit of 17,700 on prospects of good earnings.
Hankuk Glass gained 1,400 won to 19,000 for similar reasons.
